candidates.name: Kaposi's sarcoma
support_spans: A man in his 60s presented with an enlarging purpuric patch
centrally eroded purpuric plaque with multifocal peripheral reddish-purple patches, papules, and macules
candidates.why: The patient's presentation of a purpuric patch with rapid growth and extension, followed by central ulceration and bleeding, is consistent with Kaposi's sarcoma.

candidates.name: Angiosarcoma
support_spans: Dermis permeated by irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells
candidates.why: The biopsy findings of irregular, slitlike spaces containing erythrocytes and lined by plump oval cells are suggestive of Angiosarcoma.

candidates.name: Hemangioma
support_spans: Cells had pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei
Cells stained positively with CD31
candidates.why: The presence of cells with pale eosinophilic cytoplasm and hyperchromatic nuclei, and positive staining for CD31, are consistent with Hemangioma.

candidates.name: Mycosis fungoides

candidates.name: Lymphoma

candidates.why: The absence of lymphadenopathy does not rule out Lymphoma, which can present with skin lesions.
